page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes a 1890 GB local storage disk and supports Premium Storage.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor features a large 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8) for accelerated matrix operations, and SHA_NI for cryptographic workloads. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong performance, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 54,563.93 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 36.5 GB/sec, placing it in the top tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached a strong 231.56 GB/sec.

Memory performance is characterized by a read-only cached small-block bandwidth of 2,684.62 GB/sec and an uncached large-block write bandwidth of 65.26 GB/sec. For artificial intelligence workloads, the CPU's AMX instructions support strong prompt processing speeds, reaching 3,133.77 tokens/sec on a small 135M model and 219.58 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model, though text generation speeds for larger models scale down to 2.81 tokens/sec for a 70B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32ds_v7 offers a balanced resource density, combining high-frequency dedicated compute cores with substantial local storage and memory without the premium cost of specialized GPU hardware. This profile makes the instance highly suitable for relational databases, static web serving (benchmarked at a strong 59.6 GB/sec), medium-scale data processing, and CPU-based machine learning inference.

It features 128.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 1890 GB local storage disk. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmarks indicate strong performance across cryptographic, compression, and database operations, alongside high-throughput static web serving at 59.6 GB/sec.
